note: The post has only two pass-mark numbers (70 and 60), too few for 3 bars in one unit.
title: A pass mark marks the floor, not the score of a good candidate
takeaway: Anchor the number to the job or to people already doing it, or start at a moderate default and check it after the first cohort.
sources: Someone picks 70% because it sounds reasonable, and from then on it silently decides who you never meet.
It is slow, but it anchors the number to the job instead of to a feeling.
Your pass mark should sit comfortably below the score of people you would hire again.

data.caption: Three ways to set a pass mark
rows: Sum of odds a minimally competent pass
Slow, but anchored to the job
Needs a group already in the role
Start at 60, revisit after a cohort
Check it once 30 or more have sat it
